response.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_iga_igm_diff FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) AS mean_diff FROM patient_averages) SELECT pa.SEX, AVG(pa.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(pa.avg_iga_igm_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(pa.avg_iga_igm_diff / NULLIF(o.mean_diff, 0)) AS avg_ratio_to_overall_mean FROM patient_averages AS pa CROSS JOIN overall AS o GROUP BY pa.SEX;

assumptions.assumption: A record contributes to the IGA−IGM average only when both values are present. Patients with no such records have a NULL difference and are excluded from the overall mean and relevant sex averages. A zero overall mean yields a NULL ratio.
